title: Strategic Expansion Offers Matrix and Technical Validation Playbook
body:
Purpose and audience:
- Short: a repeatable, technical-first playbook CS teams can use during QBRs and renewal cycles to land Dedicated upgrades, Private deployments, and premium SLA add-ons.
- Audience: CSMs, solutions engineers (SEs), account execs when escalation needed, and SRE/infra partners for technical validation.

When to use (triggers):
- Customer hits steady-state token volume > 5M/month and has latency or data isolation concerns.
- Customer requests capacity guarantees or wants to move from multi-tenant to isolated pools.
- Security/compliance asks (VPC peering, private control plane) escalate in renewal window.
- Cost-per-token reduction targets presented by customer.

Segmentation and offer mapping (short matrix):
- Tier A: High-throughput production (>= 10M tokens/mo), latency-sensitive, data-regulated -> Offer: Dedicated 1+ GPUs, SLA Bronze/Silver, private deployment evaluation.
- Tier B: Mid-scale (2M–10M tokens/mo), budget-conscious, intermittent spikes -> Offer: Dedicated burstable with autoscale policy, cost-optimization review, optional SLA Silver.
- Tier C: Early/POC (<2M tokens/mo) but strategic -> Offer: Hosted + committed discount, pilot private deployment proof-of-concept (POC) with technical success criteria.

Value messaging bullets (engineer-friendly, short):
- Dedicated: predictable tail latency, per-route capacity, KV cache locality reduces p99 by up to 35% in internal tests.
- Private: network isolation + customer KMS, audit logs; removes shared-control-plane risks for compliance.
- SLA add-ons: financial uptime guarantees and faster incident response (2hr vs 8hr).

Technical validation checklist (SE/SRE checklist to attach to QBR notes):
- Workload profile captured: avg tokens/s, peak tokens/s, sequence length distribution, percent streaming requests.
- Performance targets agreed: target p50/p95/p99 latency, throughput, acceptable cold-start window.
- Data residency & network: required regions, VPC peering ok, egress constraints, firewall rules documented.
- Storage & KV cache: expected model kv-hits ratio, prefix cache reuse opportunities.
- Auth & keys: KMS/HSM requirements captured, rotation policy, SCIM/SAML integration needs.
- Observability hooks: desired telemetry (per-route token counts), tracing ids, retention windows.
- Rollout plan: canary percents, automatic fallback model, rollback criteria.

QBR expansion conversation template (note-style prompts for CSM):
- Business recap: "Since last QBR, usage grew X% and costs trended Y; what product metrics are most important to you next quarter?"
- Technical warm-up: "Can you confirm average and peak token rates and any expected campaign spikes?"
- Opportunity framing: "Based on observed profile, a Dedicated pool could reduce unit cost by ~N% and improve p99 by M ms; would you like a numbers walkthrough?"
- Risk & mitigation: "If private deployment needed, we can run a 4‑week POC with an SE and SRE; success = p99 below threshold and no functional regressions."

Renewal / tracker snapshot (CSV-style, paste into sheet):
- account_id,account_name,current_offer,monthly_tokens,last_q_growth_pct,renewal_date,recommended_action,owner
- 10021,Acme Payments,hosted,3,200,2026-05-15,Pilot Dedicated (4w),Maya Chen
- 10038,Novara Health,dedicated,11,10,2026-07-01,Move to Private eval + SLA, Ravi Patel
- 10044,ByteScale,hosted,1,150,2026-04-30,Offer committed-discount + uplift campaign,Alicia Gomez

Pricing and ROI framing (talking points for AE/CSM):
- Show three-year run-rate comparison: hosted list vs dedicated reserved vs private (platform + infra ops). Focus on unit token economics and tail latency savings for user-facing features.
- Emphasize non-linear benefits: predictable billing, simplified incident ops, and developer velocity from stable model versions.

Customer technical POC plan (4-week template):
- Week 0: kickoff, capture SLOs, network walkthrough, sign POC scope.
- Week 1: infra provisioning (dedicated pool or private control plane), baseline latency/throughput collection on current infra.
- Week 2: model variants deployed, KV/prefix cache enabled, tuning of batching windows.
- Week 3: stress / spike testing, SLA latency validation, security audit checklist.
- Week 4: handoff, runbook, final results, decision point.

Email snippets (short):
- Outreach to schedule QBR: "Hi [name], been seeing steady usage growth — can we align for a 30m QBR to review performance and a potential Dedicated pilot that could lower your per-token costs?"
- Post-POC results: "Results attached: p95 improved by X ms, cost per 1k tokens reduced by Y%. Recommend next steps: Reserved contract or private eval."

Objections and rebuttals (quick):
- "We don't have budget": "We can start with a 4-week POC and show concrete unit-cost delta; many customers convert once ROI is proved."
- "We won't migrate infra": "Private deployment can be staged with mirror traffic; our SEs provide runbook and SRE support for the initial cutover."
- "Security concerns": "We support customer-managed KMS, SOC2 artifacts, and on-prem options for air-gapped environments; list of required docs attached in artifacts."

Success metrics to track post-offer:
- adoption_rate (conversion from pilot to paid), unit_token_cost_delta, p95_latency_delta, number_of_incidents_post_rollout, time_to_first_successful_request (post-cutover).

Operational handoffs (who to loop in):
- SE assigned for technical validation and POC.
- SRE/infra lead for capacity planning and runbook review.
- Legal for SLA terms and contract amendment.
- Solutions engineering for performance tuning.

Appendix: helpful links and templates to attach to a QBR packet:
- POC checklist (SE playbook link), network requirements template, contract amendment template, sample SLA wording, cost comparison workbook.

Notes to self / next edits:
- Add real examples from 2–3 closed expansion deals with numbers (post-review).
- Create slide deck template for exec QBR with one-page tech appendix.
- Validate estimated p99 improvements with runtime team benchmarks.

Quick wins (things CSMs can do tomorrow):
- Export last 90 days of token metrics and compute projected 12-month spend at current growth rate.
- Run a short "latency hotspots" audit with observability team and flag top 3 routes for batch/cache tuning.
- Propose a 4-week pilot with clear success criteria in the renewal email.

End of playbook.
